newsitem.title: USA: Northwestern U's Gordon urges Fed to experiment.
newsitem.headline: Northwestern U's Gordon urges Fed to experiment.

text.p: A prominent U.S. economist on Friday urged the Federal Reserve to conduct an experiment to see how low the unemployment rate can fall without spurring inflation.

"I do think there is a case to be made for the Fed taking this as a time to use the economy as a controlled experiment," Robert Gordon of Northwestern University told a symposium convened by the American Economic Association.

"There just isn't enough indication in the tea leaves ... to say that there's really a big case to be made for creating more unemployment," said Gordon, who spoke as a member of a panel moderated by Fed Gov. Laurence Meyer.

With the unemployment rate at a seven-year low of 5.1 percent, some Fed officials have become concerned that inflation could turn higher. A number of analysts believe the central bank will be concerned enough to nudge interest rates higher.
Gordon, an expert on the relationship between unemployment and inflation, said the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment, or "NAIRU," has declined in recent years.
Gordon and many other economists had previously identified an unemployment rate of around 6.0 percent as NAIRU, but he said Friday it could now be below 5.0 percent.
However, he said there were measurement problems that made it difficult to determine what the NAIRU is, which would make an experiment by the Fed useful.
He suggested that there was not enough evidence to suggest the NAIRU has already been reached.
